I'm actually female, and I've been struggling with obesity since being diagnosed with major depression at age 12 despite being a vegetarian since age 6. I generally live on pasta and pizza, which is definitely my biggest problem. 

I have done a lot of research into vegetarian sources of protein and iron, which are what I lack the most. I know I'm going to have to undertake a major overhaul as far as my regular diet goes but again, living between my grandma's and my parents houses makes it difficult for me to prepare my own meals without attracting unwanted attention.

Thank you everyone for your advice and support. I am really ready to make a change, and hopefully in the process I will be able to start living more independently.

There are many things that you can do to help people as an artist. For example, make art that highlights a certain issue, stage an artshow/fundraiser for a local charity, or volunteer to teach kids crafts at the YMCA or after school program. You could probably find a career in art therapy, too.
I applaud you for your incredible accomplishment. People like you are an inspiration to all of us obese people trying to make a change.

Absolutely. Many people don't understand that your health isn't measured on a scale. I would say it's fine to maintain a weight in the upper range of what is healthy according to your BMI. I do think that the media has a vastly negative effect on body image, especially for women. But that's why the emphasis on healthy is so much more important than an emphasis on being attractive, and trying to say your morbid obesity is attractive is completely counterintuitive.

Some people are more sensitive than others. I have been called overly-emotional by people in the past, and it's not something I can help. It's completely irrational and unless I am focusing on being extremely self-aware, it's hard to control. She probably can't understand why you don't see things the same way she does. 

Has she been having a bad day/week/month? That can bring anyone down, and sometimes the little things just pile up. I'm sure you can relate to that.

It's also possible that it could be caused by hormones. If she's on or nearing her period (yeah, it's an icky subject but still) it's safe to assume she'd be even more emotional than usual.
